pool.text: Portuguese settlers founded a small village known initially as Vila da Nossa Senhora.
The original name of the settlement was officially changed to Curitiba.
Foreigners gained legal ownership rights to land, encouraging immigration.
Curitiba officially became a town while spelling its name Curityba.
Parana became an independent province and Curitiba was declared the capital.
The Paranaguá to Curitiba railroad was officially opened for transportation.
German Jewish academics migrated to Brazil and some settled in Curitiba.
The urban design proposal known as the Curitiba Master Plan was adopted.
The Fundação Cultural de Curitiba was set up to promote culture.
The world's second bus rapid transit system was opened in the city.
The Polish Pope John Paul II visited and blessed a traditional replica house.
Tourism generated US$280 million, representing four percent of net income.
Curitiba became Brazil's first city to receive the Pole of Information Technology prize.
Curitiba received the American Capital of Culture title granted by the OAS.
The GDP reached 32 billion reals according to IPEA data.
The city placed third in a list of green cities according to Grist magazine.
Nominal GDP reached R$45.7 billion according to the IBGE.
The Global Sustainable City Award was given for sustainable urban development.
The Civic Center was listed as an urban and architectural ensemble.
Curitiba served as one of the host cities for the FIFA World Cup.
